frozen_original.title: Hegseth Restructures Military Promotions to Require Trump Loyalty
frozen_original.synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth implemented new requirements for military promotions that prioritize political loyalty to Donald Trump over merit, combat experience, and professional qualifications. The restructuring effectively installed a political loyalty test into the armed forces' advancement system, replacing the merit-based system that has governed military promotions since the post-WWII era. Retired generals and military experts warned the changes would devastate military effectiveness, drive away the most capable officers, and compromise national security.

primary.title: Unverified Allegation: Hegseth Made Trump Loyalty a Promotion Requirement
primary.description_short: The supplied claim of a Trump-loyalty test for military promotions is unverified and conflicts with cited merit-based policy language.
primary.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Hegseth changed military promotion rules in March 2025 to require loyalty to Trump. The prior notes say no directive establishing that test was found and cite DoD language describing promotion decisions as merit-based. A March 7 Hill opinion criticized a senior appointment as signaling loyalty over competence, but it does not establish a formal promotion rule. This internal draft remains unpublished.
primary.description_long: The supplied entry alleges that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth restructured military promotions in March 2025 so that loyalty to Donald Trump would outweigh merit and professional qualifications. The supplied research notes state that no credible directive or report was located establishing an explicit Trump-loyalty test. Those notes cite Department of Defense materials describing promotion and selection decisions as merit-based and a later review memorandum calling for fair, transparent, objective procedures; the cited government pages returned HTTP 403 in this run, so those descriptions remain supplied research context rather than newly accessed quotations. Exa search did return a March 7, 2025 Hill opinion passage arguing that the selection of retired Lt. Gen. Dan Caine could signal political loyalty over competency-based advancement. That commentary concerns one senior appointment and expresses an opinion; it does not establish a change to the military promotion system. Reports of senior-officer or military-lawyer removals likewise would not prove such a rule. This draft therefore preserves the original allegation only for internal review. It does not state that a loyalty test was enacted or that predicted effects on readiness occurred. The exact blocker is a missing directive, promotion instruction, or credible report documenting the alleged March rule and its scope.

frozen_original.title: Trump Reveals Golf Course Plans to Japanese PM Abe at Mar-a-Lago
frozen_original.synopsis: During Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe's visit to Mar-a-Lago on February 10-11, 2017, Trump used the occasion—billed as a summit on North Korea, trade, and bilateral relations—to discuss his private golf course business with Abe. Japanese media reported that Trump showed Abe plans for a potential Trump-brand golf course in Japan, blurring the line between presidential diplomacy and personal business promotion. The visit to Mar-a-Lago itself—where non-member guests could witness the two leaders' dinner and discussions in the semi-public dining room—drew scrutiny about security protocols and the use of a private club as an impromptu diplomatic venue. Ethics experts noted that using presidential meetings to advance personal business interests represented an unprecedented breach of the separation between the office and private gain.

primary.title: Trump and Abe Golfed at Trump National in Florida During Abe’s 2017 Visit
primary.description_short: The Feb. 11, 2017 public schedule lists Trump golfing with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter.
primary.description_medium: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed him playing golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The supplied allegation that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded course in Japan is not confirmed by that schedule and remains unverified. This correction records the same visit’s documented golf outing without asserting a business pitch.
primary.description_long: On February 11, 2017, President Donald Trump’s public schedule listed a round of golf with Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe at Trump National Golf Club in Jupiter, Florida. The schedule is the evidence for the date, participants and venue of the outing. It places the golf game within Abe’s official U.S. visit; it does not record their conversation. The frozen description alleged that Trump showed Abe plans for a Trump-branded golf course in Japan and discussed his private golf business. The accessed schedule entry records the golf outing but does not describe what the two leaders said or showed each other. Because a missing mention does not disprove a private conversation, that part remains an allegation requiring a source that reports what was shown or discussed. This corrected draft retains the same February 2017 Abe visit and the golf outing documented by the public schedule. It narrows the event to what the source states and removes claims about a Japanese course proposal, business promotion, or ethics experts’ assessment. It does not imply the outing alone established wrongdoing or that the trip produced a business agreement. Keep the original allegation unpublished unless it can be tied to a contemporaneous credible report or documentary record.
